questions.question: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, Il and Ill. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All metals are gold. All jewellery are gold. All gold are ornaments. Conclusions: I. Some ornaments are jewellery. Il. Some metals are jewellery. III. All jewellery are ornaments.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, Il and Ill. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All metals are gold.

All jewellery are gold.

All gold are ornaments.

Conclusions:

I. Some ornaments are jewellery.

Il. Some metals are jewellery.

III. All jewellery are ornaments.

options.text: Only conclusions I and Ill follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and Ill follow

options.text: Only conclusions Il and Ill follow
options.html: Only conclusions Il and Ill follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and Il follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and Il follow

questions.solution:
Conclusions

I. Some ornaments are jewellery → Follow (As, all jewellery are gold and all gold are ornaments. So, as whole jewellery comes in gold which whole comes in ornaments therefore it is definitely true.)

II. Some metals are jewellery → Does not Follow (As, all metals are gold and all jewellery are gold. So, it is possible but not definitely true)

III. All jewellery are ornaments → Follow (As, all jewellery are gold and all gold are ornaments. So, as whole jewellery comes in gold which whole comes in ornaments therefore it is definitely true.)

Here, Only conclusions I and Ill follow.

questions.question: At which Olympic Games did India win a gold medal for the first time?
questions.questionHtml: At which Olympic Games did India win a gold medal for the first time?
questions.solution: The Indian men's hockey team clinched their first Olympic gold medal in the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics. This marked the beginning of India's long dominance in the field of hockey. This historic win initiated India's golden era in hockey, with the Indian team securing six consecutive golds in the Olympics from 1928 to 1956.

questions.question: Identify the black soil region of India from the following.
questions.questionHtml: Identify the black soil region of India from the following.
questions.solution: The black soil region of India is primarily found in the Deccan Trap. Black soil, also known as Regur or Cotton Soil, is rich in minerals and ideal for growing cotton, sugarcane, and soybeans. It is prevalent in central and western parts of India, including states like Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat.

questions.question: Who is the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
questions.solution: Karnam Malleswari is the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal. She accomplished this feat during the 2000 Sydney Olympics, where she won a bronze medal in the women's 54 kg weightlifting category. This landmark achievement marked a significant milestone in the history of Indian women participating in international sports events.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Union Public Service Commission? 1. The Parliament has the power to make regulations as to conditions of service of the Chairman, members and staff of the commission. 2. The Government of India Act, 1935, envisaged a Public Service Commission for the Federation and a Provincial Public Service Commission for each Province or group of Provinces. 3. The Federal Public Service Commission came to be known as the Union Public Service Commission by virtue of Clause (1) of Article 378 of the Constitution in 1950.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Union Public Service Commission?

1. The Parliament has the power to make regulations as to conditions of service of the Chairman, members and staff of the commission.

2. The Government of India Act, 1935, envisaged a Public Service Commission for the Federation and a Provincial Public Service Commission for each Province or group of Provinces.

3. The Federal Public Service Commission came to be known as the Union Public Service Commission by virtue of Clause (1) of Article 378 of the Constitution in 1950.
questions.solution: According to Article 318 of the Indian Constitution, the President of India and not the Parliament has the power to determine the conditions of service of the Chairman and other members of the UPSC. Hence, Statement A is incorrect. The Government of India Act, 1935, envisaged a Public Service Commission for the Federation and a Provincial Public Service Commission for each Province or group of Provinces. The Federal Public Service Commission came to be known as the Union Public Service Commission by virtue of Clause (1) of Article 378 of the Constitution in 1950. Both statements B and C are correct.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution talks about ‘abolition of title’?
questions.questionHtml: Which Article of the Indian Constitution talks about ‘abolition of title’?
questions.solution: Article 18 of the Indian Constitution discusses the 'abolition of titles'. Within this article, it is expressed that the State cannot confer any titles, and citizens of India cannot accept titles from a foreign State. This Article is integral to the principle of equality that the Constitution of India strongly advocates.

questions.questionHtml: The authorities of which country denied the permission to land the ship Komagata Maru, carrying Indians?
questions.solution: The Komagata Maru incident revolves around the Japanese steamship named Komagata Maru, which was filled with Indian passengers and denied entry into Canada in 1914. Canadian authorities refused to allow the passengers to disembark when the ship arrived at Vancouver's Burrard Inlet in late May 1914.

questions.question: During which festival is Garba performed?
questions.questionHtml: During which festival is Garba performed?
questions.solution: Garba is a popular folk dance native to Gujarat, a state in western India. Its performance is central to Navratri celebrations in Gujarat and is now popular all over India and among Indian communities worldwide.

questions.question: In December 2021, the Supreme Court suspended OBC quotas for local body elections in which of the following states?
questions.questionHtml: In December 2021, the Supreme Court suspended OBC quotas for local body elections in which of the following states?
questions.solution: In December 2021, the Supreme Court of India suspended the OBC (Other Backward Classes) quota in local body elections. The states affected were Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. This ruling translates to the fact that state election commissions can no longer reserve seats for OBCs in all future local body elections across India.

questions.question: How many industries were listed in Schedule A of Industrial Policy, 1956?
questions.questionHtml: How many industries were listed in Schedule A of Industrial Policy, 1956?
questions.solution: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 in India classified industries into three categories: Schedule A, B, and C. There were 17 industries listed under Schedule A. Some of the sectors under Schedule A included arms and ammunition, atomic energy, iron and steel, heavy machinery, mineral oil, coal, etc.

questions.question: What cells help In osmoregulation In platyhelminthes?

questions.question: Malik Ambar, who resisted Mughals in Deccan, was an able administrator of which state?
questions.questionHtml: Malik Ambar, who resisted Mughals in Deccan, was an able administrator of which state?

questions.question: Ferns, horsetails and lycophytes belong to which of the following groups?
questions.questionHtml: Ferns, horsetails and lycophytes belong to which of the following groups?
questions.solution: Ferns, horsetails, and lycophytes all belong to the group referred to as Pteridophyta. These represent some of the earlier forms of vascular plants on Earth. They are classified as a subdivision of the plant kingdom, known as cryptogams, which do not produce seeds or flowers.

questions.question: The Ashtadhyayi of Panini is a renowned work on _______.
questions.questionHtml: The Ashtadhyayi of Panini is a renowned work on _______.
questions.solution: Ashtadhyayi, also known as Astadhyayi, is a renowned work on Sanskrit Grammar. This treatise was written by the ancient Indian grammarian Panini between the 6th and 5th century BC. Ashtadhyayi is composed of approximately 4,000 sutras and is organized into eight chapters, hence the name "Ashtadhyayi," which translates to "Eight Chapters."

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about surface tension?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about surface tension?

options.text: Surface tension is typically measured in dynes/cm.
options.html: Surface tension is typically measured in dynes/cm.

options.text: The shape of water drop is spherical due to surface tension.
options.html: The shape of water drop is spherical due to surface tension.

options.text: At room temperature, surface tension of water is less than ethyl alcohol.
options.html: At room temperature, surface tension of water is less than ethyl alcohol.

options.text: The cohesive forces between liquid molecules are responsible for the phenomenon known as surface tension.
options.html: The cohesive forces between liquid molecules are responsible for the phenomenon known as surface tension.

questions.solution: Contrary to statement 3, at room temperature, the surface tension of water is actually higher than that of ethyl alcohol. For example, water at 20°C has a surface tension of 72.8 dynes/cm, while that for ethyl alcohol is 22.3 dynes/cm. The cohesive forces between liquid molecules are indeed responsible for the phenomenon known as surface tension. These forces cause the liquid to behave as though it is covered with a stretched elastic sheet, a property known as surface tension

questions.question: In which year was the Vernacular Press Act enacted in British India?
questions.questionHtml: In which year was the Vernacular Press Act enacted in British India?
questions.solution: The Vernacular Press Act was enacted in British India in the year 1878. This law was enforced by the British to curtail the freedom of the Indian-language press. The Act was used to prevent the expression of criticism toward British policies, notably, the opposition that had grown with the outset of the Second Anglo-Afghan War (1878-80). The Act was, however, repealed in 1882 by Lytton's successor, Lord Ripon, in a move to foster press freedom in India.

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 400 m. When the policeman starts chasing, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 32 km/h and that of the policeman is 40 km/h, then how far would the thief have run before he is overtaken?
questions.questionHtml: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 400 m. When the policeman starts chasing, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 32 km/h and that of the policeman is 40 km/h, then how far would the thief have run before he is overtaken?
questions.solution:
Distance = relative speed × time ⇒ 400 = (40 - 32) × (5/18) × time ⇒ Time = (400 × 18)/40 = 180 sec

Distance travelled by thief = 32 × (5/18) × 180 ⇒ 32 × 5 × 10 = 1600 m

questions.question: Raj’s income is Rs. 45,000 and his expenditure is Rs. 33,000. If his income is increased by 20% and expenditure by 12%, then what will be the percentage increase in saving?
questions.questionHtml: Raj’s income is Rs. 45,000 and his expenditure is Rs. 33,000. If his income is increased by 20% and expenditure by 12%, then what will be the percentage increase in saving?
questions.solution:
Saving = (45000 - 33000) = Rs.12000

Increment of 20% in income = 45000 × 120% = Rs.54000 ; Increment of 12% in expenditure = 33000 × 112% = Rs.36960

New saving = (income - expenditure) ⇒ (54000 - 36960) = Rs.17040

% increment = {(17040 - 12000) × 100}/12000 = (5040 × 100)/12000 = 42%

questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first and the last sentences (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up and named P, Q, R, S. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

(S1) Today, the world has become a much smaller place, thanks to the adventures and miracles of science.

(P) We are slowly realising that the world is a single cooperative group.

(Q) Other religions have become forces with which we have to reckon, and we are seeking for ways and means by which we can live together in peace and harmony.

(R) Mingling of population is bringing about interchange of thought.

(S) Foreign nations have become our next-door neighbours.

(S6) We cannot have religious unity and peace so long as we assert that we are in possession of the light and all others are groping in the darkness.
questions.solution: The rising interconnection and global character of the world are discussed in sentence S. Sentence R discusses how population mixing results in an exchange of ideas, which is pertinent to the subject. Sentence P expands on the notion that the world is shrinking by describing how it is uniting into a single cooperative community. Sentence Q discusses the necessity of religious unity and peace, which is an issue that is pertinent in the globalised world of today.
